page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.large is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, and is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the shared CPU allocation limits performance. The instance scored 1107.98 in stress-ng single-core CPU testing, placing it in the bottom 25% tier, and 2199.5 in multi-core testing, which falls into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers registering at 17.08 GB/sec. Computational tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10% tier, while database operations like Redis SET operations achieved 3.0 million operations per second.

The ecs.n4.large offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high network throughput. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU model, which can lead to resource contention and variable performance under sustained loads. Given the lack of local storage, baseline network bandwidth, and lower benchmark scores across CPU and memory tests, this instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development or testing environments, and simple background tasks.
